examples.en: My father is an owner-driver taxi driver.
I make my living running a private taxi.
An owner-driver taxi doesn't belong to a company.
At night it's hard to catch an owner-driver taxi.
I took a private taxi all the way to the airport.
The private taxi driver knows the roads well.

explain: 회사 소속이 아니라 기사 본인이 면허를 가지고 운행하는 택시예요. 회사에서 운영하는 '법인택시'와 구분해서 말해요. 보통 '개인택시 기사'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a taxi run by a driver who holds the license personally, not by a company. It is distinguished from '법인택시', which a company operates. People usually say '개인택시 기사'.

examples.en: I write down each day's schedule in my notebook.

examples.ko: 저는 그날그날 기분에 따라 옷을 골라요.
examples.en: I pick my clothes depending on my mood each day.

examples.ko: 오늘 할 일은 그날그날 끝내는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to finish each day's tasks on that same day.
Vegetable prices at the market differ from day to day.

examples.ko: 그날그날 배운 단어를 복습하면 잊어버리지 않아요.
examples.en: If you review the words you learn each day, you won't forget them.

examples.ko: 그날그날 먹고 싶은 음식을 골라서 먹어요.
examples.en: I choose and eat whatever I feel like eating each day.

explain: '매일'은 날마다 반복된다는 느낌이고, '그날그날'은 그날의 사정이나 기분에 맞춰 하루하루 달라진다는 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 '달라요, 다르다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '그때그때'도 있어요.
explain_en: '매일' stresses that something repeats every day, while '그날그날' means day by day, adjusting to that day's situation or mood. That is why it often appears with '달라요' (is different). A similar word is '그때그때' (depending on each moment).

examples.en: This café has a lot of regular customers.
The owner gave a free extra to a regular customer.
I'm a regular customer at this hair salon.

examples.ko: 단골손님 덕분에 우리 가게가 계속 문을 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to our regulars, our shop can stay open.
We warmly welcomed a regular who came for the first time in a while.
I went so often that I'm now treated as a regular.

explain: 가게 쪽에서 손님을 부를 때 많이 써요. 손님이 말할 때는 '여기 단골이에요'처럼 '단골'만 써도 되고, 자주 가는 가게는 '단골집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Shops often use it when talking about their customers. A customer can simply say '여기 단골이에요' using '단골' alone, and a place you visit often is a '단골집'.

examples.en: I steamed a kabocha squash and ate it as a snack.
I peeled the skin to make kabocha soup.
This kabocha is sweet and soft.
Kabocha was on sale at the mart, so I bought one.
I boiled kabocha and potatoes together.
You can also make a cake with kabocha.

explain: '애호박'은 연한 초록색이어서 찌개나 전에 넣고, 단호박은 껍질이 단단하고 속이 노랗고 달아요. 그냥 '호박'은 이 둘을 포함해 여러 호박을 부르는 말이에요. '단'은 '달다'에서 온 말이에요.
explain_en: '애호박' is pale green and goes into stews and pancakes, while 단호박 has a hard skin and a sweet yellow inside. Plain '호박' is the name covering both and other kinds. The '단' comes from '달다' (sweet).

examples.en: A ball flew over and hit me on the head.
A baby's head is very round.
My head is big, so hats do not fit.
A big bump appeared on my head.
I bought a watermelon as big as a head.
That kid has a nicely shaped head.

explain: '머리'를 낮추거나 장난스럽게 말하는 느낌이에요. 어른에게 쓰지 않고, 가까운 사이에서 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요. 보통은 그냥 '머리'라고 해요.
explain_en: It sounds like a lowered or playful way of saying '머리'. Do not use it with elders; it is for light teasing between close people. Normally you just say '머리'.

examples.en: This cafe has a modern interior.
I bought a chair with a modern design.
I want to decorate my room in a modern style.
It is so modern that it looks a bit cold.
It is a modern and neat house.
The building that used to look modern looks old now.

explain: 모던하다는 디자인, 인테리어, 옷처럼 취향을 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 말 '현대적이다'는 더 딱딱해서 글에 어울려요.
explain_en: Modeonhada is used for taste in design, interiors, and clothes. The similar 'hyeondaejeogida' is stiffer and suits writing.

examples.ko: 아기 새가 어미가 주는 먹이를 받아먹어요.
examples.en: The baby bird takes and eats the food its mother gives.

examples.ko: 동생은 제가 주는 과자를 넙죽 받아먹었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling eagerly took the snack I gave and ate it.

examples.ko: 강아지가 손에서 간식을 받아먹는 모습이 귀여워요.
examples.en: It's cute to see the puppy take a treat from my hand and eat it.

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 아이들이 혀를 내밀고 눈을 받아먹으려고 했어요.
examples.en: When it snowed, the kids stuck out their tongues to catch the snow.

examples.ko: 아이가 이유식을 잘 받아먹고 낮잠을 잤어요.
examples.en: The baby ate the baby food well and then took a nap.

examples.ko: 남이 사 주는 밥만 받아먹지 말고 이제 제가 살게요.
examples.en: I won't just keep accepting meals bought for me, now I'll pay.

explain: 그냥 '먹다'와 달리 누가 주는 것을 받아서 먹는다는 뜻이 들어 있어요. 아기, 새, 강아지가 먹여 주는 것을 먹을 때 자주 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 '얻어먹다'와 비슷하게 남이 사 주는 것을 먹는 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '먹다', it carries the idea of receiving something given and then eating it. It's often used for babies, birds and puppies being fed. About a person, it can also feel close to '얻어먹다', eating what others buy for you.

examples.en: This city has very well-developed transportation.

examples.ko: 아이들은 어릴 때 뇌가 빨리 발달해요.
examples.en: Children's brains develop fast when they are young.
Technology advanced and life became easier.
For muscles to develop you need exercise and sleep.
The more developed a country is, the more hospitals it has.
The internet is developing at a really fast pace.

explain: '발전하다'는 앞으로 나아가 좋아지는 큰 흐름이고, '발달하다'는 몸·기술·제도가 단계를 거치며 자라는 느낌이에요. '교통이 발달하다', '기술이 발달하다'처럼 주어가 '교통·기술·산업·근육'일 때 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 발전하다 is the big picture of moving forward and improving, while 발달하다 feels like a body, technology, or system growing step by step. It appears most often with subjects like 교통, 기술, 산업, and 근육.

p.n: 발전하다 stresses progress forward; 발달하다 stresses reaching an advanced state.

examples.en: The laundry piled up, so I washed it all at once on the weekend.
Please put the dirty laundry in the laundry basket.

examples.ko: 여행에서 돌아와 빨랫감을 한꺼번에 세탁기에 넣었어요.
examples.en: After coming back from the trip, I put all the laundry into the washing machine at once.

examples.ko: 흰색 빨랫감과 색깔 있는 옷을 따로 빨아요.
examples.en: I wash white laundry and colored clothes separately.

examples.ko: 땀에 젖은 운동복을 빨랫감에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put the sweaty workout clothes in with the laundry.

examples.ko: 빨랫감 양이 많으면 세제를 더 넣어야 해요.
examples.en: If there is a lot of laundry, you need to add more detergent.

explain: '빨래'는 빠는 일이나 빨아서 널어 둔 옷을 모두 말하고, '빨랫감'은 앞으로 빨아야 할 옷이나 천을 말해요. 그래서 '빨랫감이 쌓이다'라고 하고, '빨래를 널다/개다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '빨래' covers the act of washing and clothes already washed and hung up, while '빨랫감' is the clothes and fabric that still need washing. So you say '빨랫감이 쌓이다' (laundry piles up) but '빨래를 널다/개다' (hang up or fold laundry).

en: to wash the dishes; to do the dishes

examples.en: I wash the dishes right after dinner.
I did the dishes today.
I listen to music while I wash the dishes.
After I eat and wash the dishes, I'll clean up.
If we wash the dishes together, it finishes quickly.
Thank you for doing the dishes today.

explain: '설거지'는 식사 뒤에 그릇을 씻어 정리하는 집안일 전체를 가리켜서 '설거지를 하다'라고 많이 말해요. 컵 한 개만 씻을 때는 '컵을 씻다'라고 해요. 가족끼리 순서를 정할 때 '설거지 당번'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '설거지' names the whole chore of washing and putting away dishes after a meal, so '설거지를 하다' is very common. If you only wash one cup, say '컵을 씻다'. Families also use '설거지 당번' for whose turn it is.

examples.en: My younger sibling is still innocent.
I was innocent when I was young too.
You don't need to be that naive.
With an innocent face, he believed the lie as it was.
He is innocent and kind-hearted.
Being so naive, it is easy to get cheated.

explain: 좋은 뜻으로 '때 묻지 않았다'고 칭찬할 수도 있고, 세상 물정을 모른다는 나쁜 뜻으로도 써요. 어른에게 '순진하시네요'라고 하면 놀리는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어요. '순수하다'는 거의 칭찬이에요.
explain_en: It can be a compliment meaning unspoiled, or a criticism meaning ignorant of the world. Telling an adult '순진하시네요' can sound like teasing. '순수하다' is almost always praise.

en: to go ahead; to go before; to take the lead

examples.ko: 친구가 저보다 몇 걸음 앞서가고 있어요.
examples.en: My friend is a few steps ahead of me.
Our team stayed in the lead until the second half.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 기술에서 다른 회사보다 앞서가요.
examples.en: That company is ahead of other companies in technology.
I walked along the road following the person ahead.

examples.ko: 아이가 혼자 앞서가서 자꾸 불러야 했어요.
examples.en: The child kept going ahead alone, so I had to keep calling out.

examples.ko: 시대를 앞서가는 생각이라서 처음엔 이해하기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: It was a thought ahead of its time, so it was hard to understand at first.

explain: '앞서다'와 비슷하지만 '앞서가다'는 실제로 먼저 걸어가거나 앞에서 이끄는 느낌이 있어요. 기술이나 생각이 남보다 낫다고 할 때도 써요. 반대로 뒤에 처지는 것은 '뒤처지다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '앞서다', but '앞서가다' carries more of a feeling of actually walking ahead or leading from the front. It is also used when technology or ideas are better than others'. The opposite, falling behind, is '뒤처지다'.

examples.en: I go to sleep at a regular time every day.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 사계절 내내 가격이 일정해요.
examples.en: This shop's prices stay constant all year round.
Keep the water temperature constant.
With part-time jobs, the pay isn't steady.

examples.ko: 수업 시간이 일정해서 계획을 세우기 편해요.
examples.en: The class time is fixed, so it's easy to make plans.
If the sound is steady, it's easy to imitate.

explain: 변하지 않고 같을 때 써서 '일정한 시간', '일정하게'로 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '불규칙하다'나 '들쭉날쭉하다'예요. 소리가 같은 명사 '일정'은 스케줄이라서 '오늘 일정이 뭐예요?'처럼 뜻이 달라요.
explain_en: It describes something that stays the same, often as '일정한 시간' (a fixed time) or '일정하게' (steadily). The opposites are '불규칙하다' and '들쭉날쭉하다'. The homophone noun '일정' means a schedule, as in '오늘 일정이 뭐예요?', which is a different word.

examples.en: That child's face is full of mischief.
He looked at me with playful eyes.
Even as he gets older, his playfulness stays the same.
My younger sibling often gets scolded for being mischievous.
She answered the phone in a playful voice.

examples.ko: 장난기가 발동해서 친구를 깜짝 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: My playful side kicked in and I gave my friend a surprise.

explain: '장난기가 많다/가득하다/있다'로 자주 써요. '장난기가 발동하다'처럼 말하면 갑자기 장난치고 싶어지는 상황을 가리켜요. 나쁜 뜻이 아니라 귀엽거나 유쾌한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is often used as '장난기가 많다/가득하다/있다'. '장난기가 발동하다' describes suddenly feeling like playing a prank. It is not negative; it feels cute or cheerful.

examples.en: My younger sibling has a cold and keeps shivering.
Grandmother feels the cold especially badly in winter.

examples.ko: 아이가 너무 추워해서 담요를 덮어 줬어요.
examples.en: The child was so cold that I covered him with a blanket.

examples.ko: 그렇게 추워하지 말고 이 옷을 입어요.
examples.en: Don't shiver like that, put this coat on.

examples.ko: 고양이가 추워하는 것 같아서 난로를 켰어요.
examples.en: The cat seemed cold, so I turned on the heater.

examples.ko: 추워하던 친구가 따뜻한 차를 마시고 웃었어요.
examples.en: My friend who was feeling cold smiled after drinking hot tea.

explain: '춥다'는 내가 느끼는 감각이라 '저는 추워요'라고 해요. 다른 사람이 추워하는 모습을 말할 때는 '동생이 추워해요'처럼 추워하다를 써요. 같은 방식으로 '더워하다', '무서워하다'도 있어요.
explain_en: 춥다 is for your own feeling (저는 추워요). To describe someone else showing they're cold, use 추워하다 (동생이 추워해요). The same pattern exists in 더워하다 and 무서워하다.

examples.en: I washed my hair and dried it with a hair dryer.
The hair dryer broke, so I bought a new one.
Don't hold the hair dryer too close.
The hair dryer is in the drawer.
The air from this hair dryer is too hot.

examples.ko: 헤어드라이어만 있으면 빨리 준비할 수 있어요.
examples.en: With just a hair dryer, I can get ready fast.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '드라이어'나 '드라이기'라고 많이 말해요. 머리를 말리는 일은 '드라이하다'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: In daily life people often shorten it to '드라이어' or '드라이기'. Drying hair is also sometimes called '드라이하다'.

examples.en: My grandmother gave me a ripe persimmon.
A ripe persimmon has thin skin and is very sweet.
The persimmon ripened and turned soft.

examples.ko: 가을에 홍시 한 상자를 선물 받았어요.
examples.en: In autumn I received a box of ripe persimmons as a gift.
I was so embarrassed that my face turned red like a ripe persimmon.
I tried making jam from ripe persimmons.

explain: 단단한 '단감'과 달리 푹 익어서 말랑해진 감이에요. 껍질을 말려서 먹는 '곶감'과도 달라요. 얼굴이 빨개진 걸 '홍시처럼'이라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: Unlike the firm '단감', this is a persimmon that has ripened until soft and squishy. It is also different from '곶감', which is dried. People sometimes describe a flushed face as being 'red like 홍시'.
